title: Who shares the recent fork?
hook: Trace the branches back to a common fork.

knows: A rooted tree represents a hypothesis of shared ancestry.
doesNotKnow: A and B meet at N1 before their lineage meets C or D at the root.

misconception: Tips that are drawn nearest on the page must be most closely related.
objective: Read ancestry and sister relationships from a rooted tree.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: In this rooted tree, which tip shares the most recent common ancestor with A? A and B meet at N1 before their lineage meets C or D at the root. The diagram is a hypothetical relationship, not a dated tree or a claim that one living tip descended from another.
claims.source: Relationships follow the stipulated tree; interpretation: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/20-1-organizing-life-on-earth

claims.text: Branch lengths are not a time scale and tip letters do not denote particular species.

Recall: In a rooted phylogenetic tree, what makes two tips more closely related? Relatedness is determined by the branching pattern and the most recent common ancestor, not how close labels appear on the page.

recall.question: In a rooted phylogenetic tree, what makes two tips more closely related?
recall.why: Relatedness is determined by the branching pattern and the most recent common ancestor, not how close labels appear on the page.
